items.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999
items.q: And just as I said that, Cozy was coming out to call me or something, and he heard me say that.

ctx.x: I’m sure there was, but I’m trying to think of what it was. In fact you know Ken Burns is doing a thing, right? And they came to my house two or three years ago and they came in with a crew of ten people. My basement is about as big as their — they had things all over the place. And they interviewed me and I told this story about we were in Texas and we were playing in a place called the Seven something, and we had taken a break and I went outside to get some fresh air, it was very hot in the room even though it…

I said, “I’m getting paid to work with him, you’re a bigger jerk than I am, aren’t you?” And just as I said that, Cozy was coming out to call me or something, and he heard me say that. He says, “Marty, telephone.” So he came to grab me and he pulled me in. He says, “are you crazy?” I said, “what?” He says, “didn’t you see the size of those guys?” I said, “yeah but did you hear what they said, I mean, come on, Cozy.” And the only other thing I saw was a couple of incidences. One was we were down south some place,…

waiting and now it’s like 5 or 6:00 and the guys were getting hungry. So the manager was the white guy, Frenchie — excuse me, the ginger ale, it’s human, it’s real — so we said you know we just passed a diner about a hundred feet back there. So the guy that sold the programs, Frenchie and myself, we went there to get some food. We sat at the counter, we ate, and then we took out five or six, I don’t know, for the rest of the guys. I took orders, like when you work in an office in New York, whoever wants coffee,…
